en.name: Sorghum flour
en.summary: Sorghum flour keeps 2 months in the pantry and 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). It is milled whole and gluten-free, and the germ's oil is what limits it — a bag that smells sharp has gone, whatever the date says.
en.pantry: 2 months in an airtight container on a cool, dark, dry shelf. Sorghum is milled with the germ in, so the flour carries oil, and oil oxidises with warmth, light and air. Because sorghum is a gluten-free flour it is often kept for occasional baking rather than used weekly, which is precisely how a bag quietly goes rancid at the back of a cupboard. Fresh sorghum flour smells mild and faintly sweet, closer to plain than to wholemeal; a stale bag smells sharp and tastes bitter, which is very noticeable in a gluten-free bake where there is nothing else to hide behind.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for sorghum flour. Cold storage genuinely helps, and if you bake gluten-free only now and then it is worth the space — but only in a properly airtight container, because flour takes up moisture and fridge smells readily and a cold bag opened in a warm kitchen condenses water into itself. Given a choice between fridge and freezer, use the freezer.
en.freezer: 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is the sensible default for a flour most households use occasionally. Use an airtight tub or double bag with the air pressed out, and label it — gluten-free flours look identical once frozen and blending the wrong one into a recipe is an expensive mistake. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that; what runs out is flavour as the oil oxidises slowly even cold.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container to room temperature before opening so the flour does not take up condensation. Small quantities can go straight from frozen into a batter.
spoilage: A sharp, oily or paint-like smell instead of a mild, faintly sweet one.
Bitterness in the finished bake, very obvious in a gluten-free recipe.
Clumping or hard lumps, meaning moisture got in.
Webbing, larvae or small moths in the container.
tips: Label every gluten-free flour clearly; they are indistinguishable once frozen.
Buy small bags if you bake gluten-free only occasionally.
Store in an opaque airtight tub rather than the original bag.
Smell before baking; rancidity shows up before the date does.

faq.q: How long does sorghum flour last?
faq.a: 2 months in an airtight container in the pantry, or 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and it is the sensible default for a flour you use occasionally. Seal it airtight and label it.

faq.q: How can you tell if sorghum flour has gone off?
faq.a: Smell it. A sharp, oily note means the germ oil has gone rancid, and the bitterness is especially obvious in gluten-free baking.

zh.name: 高粱粉
zh.summary: 高粱粉密封放常溫可放 2 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 4 個月。它是整粒磨的無麩質粉，限制它的是胚芽油——一袋聞起來刺鼻的粉就是壞了，不管日期寫什麼。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐、放陰涼避光乾燥的架子，2 個月。高粱是連胚芽一起磨的，所以粉裡帶油，而油會因為溫度、光線和空氣而氧化。又因為高粱粉是無麩質粉，很多人是偶爾烘焙才用，而那正是一袋粉在櫃子深處悄悄油耗掉的典型過程。新鮮高粱粉氣味溫和、微甜，比較接近白麵粉而不是全麥粉；走味的一袋聞起來刺鼻、吃起來發苦，而在無麩質配方裡沒有別的味道可以遮掩，那股苦會非常明顯。
zh.fridge: 高粱粉沒有公布的冷藏期限。低溫確實有幫助；如果你只是偶爾做無麩質烘焙，那個位置值得空出來——但一定要用真正密封的容器，因為麵粉很會吸濕也很會吸冰箱的味道，一包冰過的粉在溫暖廚房裡打開就會自己結露。冷藏和冷凍之間，請選冷凍。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 4 個月；對多數家庭偶爾才用的粉來說，這就是合理的預設。用密封罐或套兩層袋、壓出空氣，並貼標籤——無麩質粉冷凍起來長得一模一樣，混錯一種進配方是很昂貴的錯誤。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是風味，因為油脂在低溫下仍會慢慢氧化。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋，粉才不會受潮。少量的話直接從冷凍加進麵糊也沒問題。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、帶油味或油漆味，而不是溫和微甜。
成品發苦，在無麩質配方裡特別明顯。
結塊或出現硬塊，表示受潮。
容器裡出現絲網、幼蟲或小蛾。
tips: 每種無麩質粉都要清楚標示；冷凍之後根本分不出來。
只是偶爾做無麩質烘焙的話，買小包就好。
用不透光的密封罐，不要就著原袋放。
烤之前先聞；油耗會比日期更早出現。

faq.a: 密封放常溫 2 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 4 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 4 個月；對偶爾才用的粉這是合理的預設。密封好並貼上標籤。
聞一下。刺鼻帶油味就是胚芽油耗了，而那股苦在無麩質烘焙裡特別明顯。
